purpose: Local diagnostic of the original CA allocator, not validation of a new learning policy or formal performance data
controller: Exact archived A old CA core, trajectory, speed envelope, learning rule and fault guards
event: First WITHDRAWN or CONTRACTED mask during phase 2 or later; 64 preceding task cycles, trigger cycle, 63 following cycles. Times measured, not interpolated.
noEventFallback: Last 64 cycles; trigger_ms=-1. This is NOT an observed withdrawal event.
interruptedCapture: Count may be below 128 if phase 6 arrives during capture. All rows are explicit; no invented post-event points.
activeTelemetry: Original 107-channel mapping unchanged during phases 0-5. No event replay during motion.

replay.when: phase=6, fault=0, after issuing zero commands
replay.faultPriority: Original I96-I103 fault trace preserved whenever fault!=0 or phase=9

status_I89.4: all chunks submitted and previous final UART transfer completed

replay.recordCount_I92: 64 normally without an event, 128 normally with an event
replay.triggerMs_I93: Action elapsed milliseconds, -1 means no event
replay.payload_I96_I103: Eight float32 values; event row offsets 8*chunkIndex through 8*chunkIndex+7
replay.delivery: Cursor advances on UART TC counter change. PC receipt still requires complete record/chunk indices in exported CSV. Missing chunks must not be interpolated. Final chunk repeats.

acquisition.beforeRun: Motor stopped; no added mass; original A mechanical setup; clear VOFA history before one fresh powered run
acquisition.normalStopRecording: I2=6, I22=0, I88=4421, I89=4. Keep the same stopped history another 5 seconds; typically I0>=55 seconds. Do NOT stop export at first phase=6.
acquisition.abnormal: Unexpected motion/vibration: make the apparatus safe immediately. If I2=9 or I22!=0, do not reset/re-run; preserve/export at least 5 seconds after fault for old fault replay.
acquisition.qualifications: Compilation does not validate on-device timing. Verify I43/I45/I57/I59/I70 and faults from this diagnostic record before any subsequent runs.
